tools.name: estimate_call
tools.description: Check route availability, estimated one-minute usage, and remaining allowance before dialing. Calls in Central America, Europe, North America, and South America. Calls involving any non-US/Canadian number require a paid plan. Uses the verified caller ID and destination to price the route. Uses cache

tools.name: place_call
tools.description: Place the call FROM the authenticated user's own verified phone number to accomplish a specific objective (book a table, ask a question, chase an order). A real-time voice agent handles the call, including automated phone menus and hold queues. Its default opening says who it is calling for and stat

tools.name: get_call
tools.description: Get the status and, once terminal, the structured resolution of a call started with place_call. Returns instantly by default. Pass wait_seconds (max 50) to have the server hold the request and return early on any status change — fewer round trips while a call is in progress. Terminal statuses: compl

tools.name: list_calls
tools.description: List the authenticated user's recent calls, newest first, with statuses and outcomes. Useful to recover a lost call_id or review call history. Pass the returned next_cursor as cursor to fetch the next page of older calls. next_cursor is null when no older calls remain. Omit cursor to start at the ne

tools.name: set_call_visibility
tools.description: Make a call owned by the authenticated user public or private. Calls are private by default. Only publish when the user explicitly asks: a public call exposes its objective, phone numbers, transcript, result and audio to anyone with its permanent, token-free listen_url, including live audio while in

tools.name: end_call
tools.description: End an in-progress call early. The voice agent wraps up politely ("I'll let you go, thanks!") and hangs up; the call is force-terminated if wrap-up takes more than ~10 seconds. Use when the user changes their mind or the call is no longer needed. The partial transcript and resolution are still produ

tools.name: get_phone_number
tools.description: Get the phone number connected to the authenticated user's account in E.164 format, along with its caller_id_status (verified or unverified). This is the user's own number used as outbound caller ID, not the service's SMS sending number. Takes no arguments and does not place a call or send a text.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "place_call" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "place_call" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: locale, callee_name, context, objective, to, user_name

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: place_call, get_call, list_calls · Private data: place_call, get_call, set_call_visibility · Public sink: estimate_call, get_call, set_call_visibility, get_phone_number · Destructive: get_phone_number.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: place_call, get_call, list_calls · Private data: place_call, get_call, set_call_visibility · Public sink: estimate_call, get_call, set_call_visibility, get_phone_number · Destructive: get_phone_number

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
